changes: Admit object-planner column lists and option records before invoking the callback; hold their independent scope until asynchronous planning settles.
Check cancellation immediately before and after object planning so a cancelled callback result cannot begin scanning.
Share admitted column-name collection with window planning, eliminating alias Set/Object.keys/Object.values temporaries and exposing optional scoped admission.
Use scratch child scopes for window row/vector collection and run planning so returned result ownership excludes planning lists.
Use own-property partition checks in both row window scan paths to preserve physical columns named constructor or similar prototype properties.

coverage: Pending planner success, failure and cancellation keep arguments charged through callback completion; only success opens the scanner, and every path releases reservations.
Oversized object-plan columns reject before planner invocation.
Window collector exact observed peak succeeds and one byte less rejects, covering duplicate names, Unicode, own aliases and inherited names.
Window scan regression asserts constructor is requested and receives the correct row_number values.
Full suite includes real Parquet HTTP, range fallback and window fixture tests.

remaining: Returned object/task/explain metadata still needs complete ownership integration; this change admits callback arguments, not all metadata returned by adapters.
Unscoped window/projected column collection remains in explain/task discovery where returned-plan lifetime must be addressed.
Geo-expression preparation, partition/filter scratch, compiler/converter workspace and whole-runtime memory validation remain open.
